blocks.text: Imagine a project with tasks that must be completed in a specific sequence. How can we determine this order using graph theory?

blocks.markdown: In this lesson, we will explore the concepts of connectivity and topological ordering in directed graphs. Specifically, we will learn how to identify strongly connected components (SCCs) and produce a topological order of a directed acyclic graph (DAG). Additionally, we'll see how topological ordering can be used to solve shortest path problems in DAGs efficiently.

blocks.title: Strongly Connected Component (SCC)
blocks.text: A strongly connected component of a directed graph is a maximal subgraph where every vertex is reachable from every other vertex in the subgraph.

blocks.title: Topological Sorting
blocks.text: Topological sorting of a directed acyclic graph (DAG) is a linear ordering of its vertices such that for every directed edge $uv$ from vertex $u$ to vertex $v$, $u$ comes before $v$ in the ordering.

blocks.markdown: To find SCCs, we can use algorithms like Kosaraju's or Tarjan's. These algorithms efficiently decompose a graph into its strongly connected components.

blocks.title: Finding SCCs using Kosaraju's Algorithm
blocks.prompt: Given a directed graph, find its SCCs using Kosaraju's algorithm.

steps.text: Perform a depth-first search (DFS) on the graph and store vertices in a stack according to their finish times.
Transpose the graph by reversing all edges.
Perform DFS on the transposed graph, using the stack from the first DFS to determine the order of exploration.
Each DFS tree in the transposed graph represents a strongly connected component.

blocks.answer: The SCCs are identified by the DFS trees in the transposed graph.

blocks.markdown: Topological sorting is crucial for scheduling tasks, and it can be achieved using a modified DFS or Kahn's algorithm.

blocks.title: Topological Sorting using DFS
blocks.prompt: Perform a topological sort on a given DAG using DFS.

steps.text: Initialize an empty stack to store the topological order.
Perform DFS on the graph. For each vertex, once all its adjacent vertices are visited, push it onto the stack.
Pop vertices from the stack to get the topological order.

blocks.answer: The topological order is obtained by popping vertices from the stack.

blocks.title: DAG Shortest Paths
blocks.text: In a DAG, shortest paths can be found in linear time by processing vertices in topological order and relaxing edges.
